_about: Machine-readable routing suggestions behind scripts/routing-card.py — the single authority for WHICH SEAT a job gets. Evidence and sources: model-matrix.md. 'settled' = the evidence clearly favors one seat: use it unless an allowed deviation reason applies. 'close' = reasonable seats differ by task: ask the user once per run (grouped, plain language) or, when unattended or told 'use your judgment', start from judgment_prior. Durable recon findings are promoted here; bump 'verified'.

never_request.gpt-reserve: reported Luna-class quota fallback pool (SECONDARY); not a seat to request
never_request.codex-auto-review: Codex's internal approval reviewer, not a worker seat
never_request.grok-4.7-build-fast: same class as grok-4.7 at 2x price; only when the user asks for speed

allowed_deviation_reasons: provider-down: the access check or a dispatch showed the seat unusable this session
consent: the seat's provider needs the user's consent and does not have it yet
context: the ticket exceeds the seat's context ceiling or crosses its price cliff
bar: the lead judges the seat cannot clear this ticket's quality bar (First Law) — name the specific risk; the record then tests the judgment
user: the user asked for a different seat (this session or in the prompt)
record: the performance record shows the seat failing on this task shape
tools: the ticket needs a tool or transport the seat lacks
task-fit: close-call rows only — a named strength of another listed option matters for this ticket
exempt: a behavior-exempt change needs no extra seat (review rows only)

jobs.label: Mechanical model work: bulk docstrings, annotations, extraction, scanning, repetitive edits a single command cannot do
jobs.evidence: list-price + benchmark (Luna measured, Haiku 4.5 not on v4.3)
jobs.why: Luna ~$0.02 per 4-turn dispatch vs Haiku ~$0.19 (list); small Luna tickets use the direct launcher, no wrapper (codex-workers.md).

options.plain: Claude Opus 5.5 — top overall reasoning; uses the same Claude allowance I run on

jobs.label: Architecture, ambiguous debugging, final judgment
jobs.why: judgment stays with the lead; a second frontier opinion uses opus, or Grok 4.7 cross-family; Astra and Fable only with the user's double approval

jobs.label: Independent verification of any behavior-changing change

default.note: Agent tool: subagent_type foreman-verifier, model "opus" (the agent file inherits the lead's model otherwise)

jobs.no_agent_tool: No Agent tool: use a fallback reviewer under the disclosed reduced-assurance rule (SKILL.md) — do not park.

jobs.label: Off-family read-only review when Claude built a behavior-changing change
jobs.escalate: High-risk changes (security boundaries, data migrations, anything irreversible): run Grok 4.6 at high AND a GPT-6 Sol read-only review; GPT-6 Astra only with the user's double approval this session.
jobs.why: a same-family verifier shares the builder's blind spots; Grok 4.6 is the cheapest output-light reviewer; confirm every Grok citation

jobs.label: Adversarial plan or design review, second opinions
jobs.evidence: output-price math + one live plan review
jobs.why: output-light work at the lowest output price; confirm every citation (hallucination ~34%)

jobs.label: Implementation needing more than ~200K tokens of context
jobs.why: Grok reprices the whole request 2x at 200K; Sonnet has no length surcharge

jobs.label: Merging findings from 2+ reviewers, checking cited findings (Jev recipes 1–2)
jobs.why: ~$0.0002 per call; shadow mode until a recipe graduates (jev.md)

premium_models.gpt-6-astra: Codex frontier tier, ~5x GPT-6 Sol's price per token
premium_models.fable: Claude Fable, ~2.5x Opus 5.5's price per token

premium_rule: Premium models are never used as subagents or workers unless the user approved them TWICE in this session (a yes to the ask, then a yes to one confirmation that names the model and its cost). Approval lasts only for the session, is never carried into another session, and is never inferred from a pre-approval flag. A LEAD that is itself a premium model is fine; this rule governs dispatches.
